title: SLO-weighted threshold smoothing and transparent failover adapter for quota enforcement
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Problem: Recent incidents showed that during cross-region outages our existing quota enforcer flips to conservative drop-all behavior which spikes SLO violations and creates an oscillating recovery pattern when the limiter comes back. We need a method that gracefully sheds load while preserving tenant fairness and minimizing SLO burn across regions.

Goal: Implement a transparent 'failover adapter' for quota enforcement that: (1) applies SLO-weighted threshold smoothing to admission decisions, (2) exposes a short-lived quota escrow to absorb coordinated bursts during regional handoffs, (3) runs a shadowing mode to warm KV caches and prefetch state from standby regions, and (4) coordinates with circuit breakers to avoid bulk lockstep rejections. Deliverables: design doc, prototype in inference-runtime, e2e chaos tests, dashboards showing SLO & fairness metrics, and rollout plan with canary + automatic rollback on increased SLO burn.

Design highlights and trade-offs: 
- Admission curve: use a smooth-step admission curve (sigmoid-like) that maps observed queue depth and token rate to probabilistic admission. Trade-off: smoother admission reduces oscillation but increases tail token latency under extreme stress.
- Quota escrow: temporarily borrow a bounded amount of capacity from standby regions during controlled failover. Trade-off: risk of small cross-region cost and eventual double-counting unless we reconcile with lease tokens. We will use idempotent escrow tokens with expiry and reconciliation job.
- Shadow warmup: during degraded mode, send 5% of requests in shadow to the standby limiter to populate KV caches. Trade-off: extra load on standby but reduces cold-start penalty on cutover.
- Circuit choreography: add a soft-open circuit breaker state that prevents full-open failures by allowing a throttled ramp-up based on successful admissions and observed SLOs.

Metrics to track: 99p latency, SLO violation rate (p50/p95/p99), error budget consumption, tenant fairness delta (Gini coefficient approximation), cross-region token double-counts, cost delta per-hour.

References and artifacts:
- Design doc (confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RR/Failover+Adapter+Design+(SLO-weighted+admission)
- Incident postmortem: https://incidents.redwood.ai/2026-02-11-rate-limiter-outage
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference-runtime/pull/12345
- Dashboard (grafana): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/limiter/failover-adapter-canary

Acceptance criteria: 
- Prototype passes chaos test (region failover) with <=30% relative increase in SLO burn compared to baseline and no tenant fairness regression beyond agreed threshold.
- No unbounded cross-region quota leaks observed after 1 hour of simulated failover; reconciliation job reduces escrow to zero within 2 hours.
- Canary rollout with 5% traffic shows stable admissions and graceful recovery across three simulated outage modes.
